history.period: 15th-16th century CE (one source suggests 8th century — conflict, unverified)
history.summary: This is an ARCHAEOLOGICAL rock-cut site, not a functioning temple — the CSV 'Devi Temple' label is approximate. Chabimura ('mountain of pictures', also Chakwrakma/Chakrakma) is a series of rock-cut panels carved into the near-vertical sandstone cliff face of the Devtamura hills on the bank of the Gomati river at Haakwchak/Haakchak, Amarpur subdivision, Gomati district — ~82 km from Agartala, ~30 km from Udaipur, and ~7.5-12 km from Amarpur town (sources differ on the last leg; the CSV town 'Amarpur' is therefore approximately right as the nearest town, not the exact site). CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name — corrected to Tripura. OVERLAP: an existing dataset file 'chabimura-rock-carvings-gomati' (1041.json) already covers this same site — keep-or-merge decision needed. The 37 carvings include a colossal Mahishasurmardini Durga (about 10.7 m tall and 7.7 m wide, ten-armed, carved ~10 m above the riverbed, worshipped by local tribes as Devi Chakrak-ma) plus images of Shiva, Vishnu, Kartikeya, Ganesha and others. The purpose and the artists are unknown; local tradition associates the site with the Manikya rulers. Date is disputed: most sources give 15th-16th century, one travel account says 8th century. The site is reached only by boat (from Rangamati in Amarpur) through the gorge, and also functions as an eco-tourism centre.

name: Chabimura Devi Temple
town_description: Chabimura is a remote riverside archaeological site in the Devtamura hill range of Amarpur subdivision, Gomati district, reached by boat through a forested gorge of the Gomati river. The nearest town is Amarpur, about 7.5-12 km away; Amarpur itself is a small subdivision town on the river route between Udaipur and the interior hills.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~82 km)
travel.railway: Agartala railway station (~82 km; nearest railhead)
travel.road: Road to Rangamati (Amarpur), then boat down the Gomati river gorge to the carvings; 30 km from Udaipur, 7.5-12 km from Amarpur
